accessibility.text: What C++ adds an iterator: an object that marks a position in a container. It behaves like a pointer into an array.
begin() marks the first element. end() marks the position one past the last, not the last element.
A loop runs while the iterator has not reached end().
*it reads or writes the element. ++it moves on. This is lecture 3's pointer arithmetic with a safer wrapper.
The range-based for loop is shorthand for exactly this loop.
The full type is long, which is what auto is for.
v[i] only makes sense for containers with numbered positions. A linked list or a map has none, yet you still need a way to say \"this element\" and \"the next one\".
iterator
end
